The first step in any business is not the product.

Kevin explains the idea with the story of how Campbell started canning soup. People loved soup but did not want to spend hours making it.

Shipping the water cost too much, so Campbell condensed the soup and let the customer add water at home. He found a market first, then filled it. Kevin calls it find a need and fill it.

What need around you is nobody filling yet?

#ad #business #success

Experience is the best teacher, but only in one case.

Kevin explains that it is true only when the experience belongs to somebody else. Why repeat every mistake he made?

He says he has been to the top of the mountain and knows the roadblocks, the disaster areas and where the road is washed out.

Learning from someone who already walked the path can save years of pain.

Whose experience could you borrow today?

#ad #success #mindset #kevintrudeau

Why every failure is a lesson, not a loss.

Kevin shares that he made plenty of mistakes early in his career and lost a lot along the way. What mattered was that he learned something from every failure.

He quotes Rockefeller: in every adversity are the seeds of a greater benefit, and you have to find them. Then he tells the Edison story: not 10,000 failures, but 10,000 ways that did not work.

What was your last failure really trying to teach you?
